text: The 3/4 hard-rich gold-first local FAILURES are OUR harness, not the tasks: test-env dependency VERSION DRIFT, cheaply fixable, scorer intact. The KB replay engine (kblib/replay.py ReplayEngine._run_pytest) runs every task's tests with one shared .venv (sys.executable) with NO per-task dependency install. rich tests hard-code exact ANSI/pygments byte output, so a pygments newer than the version a task's own poetry.lock pins makes unrelated (and for rich_4079 the target) tests fail even though the gold code is correct. MEASURED by re-running the real engine: each gold passes clean (exit 0, 0 fail/err, required_pass, harness_like) when pygments matches that task's lock pin (rich_3469->2.17.2, rich_4070/4079->2.19.2); no single global pygments satisfies all three. FIX: per-task dependency pinning (install the task's locked pygments + markdown-it-py into the checkout env before its tests) = standard SWE-bench per-instance-env practice; keeps the same FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS required-node set, JUnit validation, and zero-failure bar (does NOT weaken the scorer). IMPLICATION: 'the agent couldn't solve rich_4079/4070' was partly measured against a mis-provisioned local scorer; a per-task-pinned local eval is a prerequisite for trusting the decode sweep / LoRA / router offline. Report: Gemma/kb/audits/2026-10-15-hard-rich-gold-local-failure.md.

text: A fresh-context, TOOL-LESS reviewer/critic agent is NOT worth building for this competition (addressable failure mass ~0.7%). User ran a ~2-min offline test over the 34 measured wrong_content rich cases: exactly 1/34 (3%) carries a divergence signal a tool-less reviewer could use; the other 33 (97%) edit the symbols the issue names, in the files gold edits, and are still wrong -> only test EXECUTION detects them, which a tool-less reviewer lacks. Addressable share of total measured failure mass = 1/149 traced rich rows (~0.7%). METHOD CAUTION recorded: naive signals gave 100% (vacuous: 'covers <50% of gold lines' and 'edited same file as gold' are TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION of the WRONG-FIX label -> restate the label) and 38% (false positives from counting PROSE words a code diff naturally lacks; e.g. rich_3535 edits the exact gold regex line, \u0020-\u007e vs gold \u0020-\u006f, a 1-char Unicode-range error, but S1 fired on prose-vocab absence). Only after restricting S1 to code symbols (dotted/snake/Camel/ALLCAPS) and material-size diffs did it collapse to 1/34 then 0/34. Do NOT spend GPU on a reviewer lever.

text: WRONG-FIX in this competition is a FIX-CORRECTNESS failure, not an ask-comprehension or localization failure: the model reaches the file+symbol the issue/gold names and writes the WRONG EDIT CONTENT. Evidence: of 34 measured wrong_content cases, 33 edit gold's symbols in gold's files and still fail (only execution detects the error); rich_3535 misses by one char in a Unicode range on the exact gold-edited line; rich_4079 produced diffs up to 5.5x gold's size and still failed (size/effort is not the lack). This is distinct from the COMMITMENT/search-death failure (never reaching an edit) and from LOCALIZATION (wrong file). IMPLICATION: the LoRA/offline target is correct edit CONTENT on this code (not commit-timing alone, not localization, not a reviewer); and it is only measurable with a WORKING per-task-pinned local scorer (see J-local-gold-pygments-drift). Sharpens, does not contradict, the commitment finding: commitment gets you TO an edit; content-correctness decides whether it passes.

text: ADAPTER-LOADS-AND-TAKES-EFFECT-IN-SCORING is CONFIRMED by Kaggle staff (Ryan Holbrook, competition forum, ~2026-10-15), resolving the long-standing log contradiction (READ-THIS-FIRST said 'verified' vs detailed entries 'unconfirmed, do the probe') in favor of CONFIRMED. Host facts: (1) adapters load and ARE active in the forward pass; a competitor's 'no effect' repro was a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not an inert adapter -- at temperature 0 with p1~=0.9999, a ~1.6-nat RAW-LOGIT shift appears as only ~1e-5 on the top-1 logprob due to softmax saturation (d ln p1 / d z1 = 1-p1 ~= 1e-5 near saturation); the runner-up (top_logprobs) tokens shifted the full ~1.1-1.6 nats, proving the adapter changed logits. (2) The SCORING environment uses the SAME patched vLLM 0.19.1 wheelhouse as the local Kaggle setup -> a LOCAL adapter-effect test is a faithful proxy for scored behavior (breaks the 'can only validate by spending a scored slot' deadlock). (3) The sample submission applies LoRA to LAYER 0 ONLY (layers_to_transform:[0], target_modules:[q_proj,o_proj]); Gemma 4's Sandwich-RMSNorm + Q-RMSNorm (post_attention_layernorm between o_proj and the residual add; per-head q_norm after qkv) RENORMALIZES a single-layer perturbation away, so a 1-layer adapter shows ~no greedy-text change even with large weights. DESIGN RULE: adapt MANY layers (all 60, or a broad span), not layer 0, and expect q_proj/o_proj-into-renorm to be damped -- consider targeting more modules / MLP. STATUS: facts (1)-(3) are HOST-ASSERTED external intel (forum, treat as untrusted-but-high-signal); the softmax-saturation math is independently checkable and correct; before spending Colab, confirm locally via eval_hf_adapter that a multi-layer adapter changes greedy output on the SAME wheelhouse. This REVIVES the LoRA path: the two gates that parked it (train on 80GB [user HAS Colab] + adapter-loads-in-scoring [now host-confirmed]) are BOTH cleared.

text: A MULTI-LAYER adapter already DEMONSTRABLY takes effect on the SCORED 31B stack from on-disk runs -- the Colab adapter-effect probe is REDUNDANT as an existence test. Natural A/B: v2_gate_out served the competition SAMPLE layer-0 stub (adapter_config.json byte-equivalent to Gemma/comp_files/adapter_config.json: r4/alpha8/layers_to_transform:[0]/q_proj,o_proj; weights 217,672 B) and behaved baseline-like (edits on 5/5, rich_4077 RESOLVED); v2_gate_out2 served a 410-module multi-layer adapter (r32/alpha64, 979,558,760 B) on the SAME stack and produced tool_calls=0, patch_chars=0, end_reason=NUDGE_EXHAUSTED on 5/5. So multi-layer adapters have a LARGE effect; the open question is NOT 'does it load/take effect' but 'at what span/rank/STRENGTH does it help instead of OVERBAKE'. CORRECTS prior claims: (a) 'v2 was near-inert partly due to layer-0' is FALSE -- v2 was 410-module multi-layer and over-STRONG, not inert; the host's layer-0 renorm rule explains the SAMPLE STUB, which v2_gate_out happened to ship, not the trained v2. (b) The probe/eval_hf_adapter path can't test the wheelhouse anyway: eval_hf_adapter.py hardcodes BASE=google/gemma-4-E2B-it, 4-bit HF in-process, no vLLM, not the 31B. (c) There is NO local 31B agent: run_local.py drives a 12B GGUF stand-in; a 31B adapter can't serve on it; rp-4 scores PATCHES not agent runs. So the 'LOCAL no-adapter vs LOCAL adapter' baseline the recipe named has no stack -- the first trustworthy judge is the FREE Kaggle rich gate. (d) rp-4 gold-first validity currently covers 4 rich tasks (3469,4070,4076,4079), not 48, so a held-out EASY+HARD bar can't be scored until each task's gold is made VALID.
